statement: For the associated influence-cell dynamical system in general position with positive initial weights, prove that one weight tends to $1$ if $\alpha>1$ or $0<\beta<2\alpha$, while if $0<\alpha<1$ and $\beta>2\alpha$ all weights converge to positive limits independent of the initial values.
technical_review: Two parameter regions and every positive initial vector are quantified; the influence-cell vector field and general-position assumptions are absent. No Lyapunov function controlling both monopoly and coexistence has been established.

statement: Prove that every bounded-degree transient hyperbolic graph contains a transient subtree.
technical_review: Every bounded-degree transient hyperbolic graph is required. A geodesic spanning tree need not preserve electrical transience; no finite resistance flow supported on a subtree has been constructed.

statement: Let $H_k$ be a $k$-regular planar triangulation. At the critical percolation parameter for the event that an open cluster contains a full infinite binary tree, prove that the event has positive probability.
technical_review: The binary-tree event is evaluated at its own threshold, not ordinary percolation criticality. Supercritical branching comparisons do not show endpoint positivity; k and the meaning of embedded full binary tree need primary definitions.

statement: Prove that Bernoulli percolation has at most one infinite cluster on every bounded-degree graph roughly isometric to $\mathbb{Z}^d$.
technical_review: All bounded-degree graphs roughly isometric to every lattice dimension are quantified. Translation invariance needed by the usual uniqueness argument is absent; no replacement finite-energy counting argument is supplied.

statement: For bounded-degree graphs, prove that the property $p_c<p_u$ is invariant under rough isometry.
technical_review: The strict threshold gap must transfer both ways for every rough-isometric bounded-degree pair. Coarse geometry does not directly transport independent edge states or uniqueness thresholds.

statement: Prove that every bounded-degree graph roughly isometric to a nonamenable Cayley graph is non-Liouville.
technical_review: Requires nonconstant bounded harmonic functions on every rough-isometric graph. Nonamenability and positive spectral gap alone do not supply an audited Poisson-boundary transfer mechanism.

statement: Give general conditions implying $p_u(G)<1$. In particular, prove or disprove that every one-ended transitive graph has $p_u(G)<1$.
technical_review: General sufficient conditions plus the entire one-ended transitive class are requested. A proof for a particular lattice or group would not settle that class.

statement: (T. Stanford) The Dogolazky-Kneissler 2-torsion element in A(↓↓, Z) (see Figure 7) can be embedded into a chord diagram in A(S1, Z) in many ways. Such an embedding will always produce an element x∈A (S1, Z) with 2x = 0. Is it possible to produce such an x which is nontrivial? If so, this would give a counterexample to Conjecture 2.3. 2.2 Do Vassiliev invariants distinguish knots?
technical_review: Nonzero integral chord-diagram torsion after a closure embedding is required. Figure 7 and the integral relations are essential; mod-2 linear algebra cannot certify nonzero integral order-two torsion by itself.

statement:
Prove or disprove the conjecture about the non-uniqueness of minimal
representative of a free link, i.e. there exists a free link having
several minimal representatives.
technical_review: Existence of multiple minimal representatives is meaningful only modulo the source equivalences. A pair of diagrams with equal crossing number does not prove minimality or inequivalence.

statement: LetY be any finite cover of Mg, and let f:Y →Y be a finite order homeo- morphism. If f is homotopic to the identity, must f equal the identity?
technical_review: Every finite cover and every finite-order identity-homotopic homeomorphism are quantified. Asphericity alone does not prove pointwise rigidity; a full finite-action rigidity theorem is needed.

statement: Suppose C∞(Hom(π,G )/G) D− →C∞(Hom(π,G )/G) is a diﬀerential operator which commutes with the ModΣ-action on Hom(π,G )/G. Then D is a scalar multiple of the identity operator.
technical_review: The group G, surface and smooth structure of the character quotient are not specified in the excerpt. Ergodicity controls invariant order-zero functions but not automatically higher-order differential symbols.

statement: (Billiards in general polygons). Does every billiard table have at least one regular periodic trajectory? If the answer is aﬃrmative, does this trajectory persist under deformations of the billiard table? If a periodic trajectory exists, find the asymptotics for the number of periodic trajectories of bounded length as a function of the bound. Describe the behavior of a generic regular billiard trajectory in a generic polygon; in particular, prove (or disprove) the assertion that the billiard flow is ergodic. 1 We note that the case of triangles is already highly non-trivial. For recent work on billiards in obtuse triangles see [ Sc1] and [ Sc2]. In the case of triangles the notion of generic can be interpreted as follows. The space of triangles up to similarity can be parametrized as the set of triples ( θ1,θ 2,θ 3) with ∑θi =π and eachθi> 0. It is naturally an open simplex. Generic then refers to the natural Lebesgue measure. To motivate the next problem we note that there is a close connection between the study of interval exchange transformations and billiards in rational polygons (defined below). An important technique in the study of interval exchange maps is that of renormalization. Given an interval exchange on the unit interval one can take the induced transformation on a subinterval. The resulting map is again an interval exchange map, and if one renormalizes so that the new interval has length one, then this gives a transformation on the space of unit interval exchange maps. This transformation is called the Rauzy-Veech induction ([ Ra], [ V e2]), and it has proved to be of fundamental importance. There is a corresponding notion for the renormalization of translation surfaces given by the Teichm¨ uller geodesic flow.
technical_review: Includes existence, persistence, counting asymptotics and generic ergodicity for arbitrary polygons. Rational-polygon or acute-triangle examples are parameter instances only; no joint full-scope route.

statement: A module is **serial** if it is a direct sum of uniserial modules, and **uniserial** if its lattice of submodules is totally ordered. The question was whether every direct summand of a serial module is again serial. The report states that the answer is no: Puninski constructed a counterexample, indeed over every exceptional uniserial ring.
technical_review: The literal statement itself reports Puninski counterexamples over every exceptional uniserial ring. No new open theorem is proposed; the actual counterexample body was not replayed.

statement: Prove that the vacuum $G_2$ silent-boundary (SB) system has oscillatory behavior analogous to the oscillatory behavior proved for the Bianchi IX system.
technical_review: The full vacuum G2 silent-boundary flow needs its constraints and an oscillatory asymptotic theorem. Similarity to Bianchi IX does not transfer the dynamics or establish a short certificate.

statement: Is the identity $X_iX_j\theta(x)=X_iX_j\theta(x^{-1})$ valid in Carnot groups of higher step for mollifiers $\theta$ satisfying $\theta(x)=\theta(x^{-1})$?
technical_review: Primary report p.1880, equation (5), read with its step-two regularization argument. Inversion symmetry of a function must be distinguished from equality of left-invariant derivatives evaluated at inverse points. General inversion exchanges left/right fields; the report does not specify enough mollifier structure here to certify a counterexample. No new claim or successor-body clearance.

statement: Assume $AD^+$ and that there is no $\d714_1$-iteration strategy for a mouse with a superstrong cardinal. Let $\varphi(v)=\exists A\subseteq\mathbb{R}\,\psi(A,v)$ be a $\Sigma^1_2$ formula, where $\psi$ has $k$ real quantifiers, and let $x\in\mathbb{R}$. If $\varphi(x)$ is true, then there is a mouse $N$ over $x$ such that $N$ is a $\langle\varphi,x\rangle$-witness.
technical_review: The strategy symbol is corrupted and witness mouse is undefined. All real parameters and existential real-set formulas are quantified; constructing witnesses requires substantial inner-model theory, not a finite model check.

statement: In the report’s setup, where \a0\(D\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a bounded open set and \(\hat\Omega\subset D\) is an optimal set for minimizing the \(k\)-th Dirichlet-Laplacian eigenvalue under a volume constraint, for \(k\ge 3\), assuming \(D\) is connected, can one prove or disprove the (Lipschitz-)continuity of the associated eigenfunctions?
technical_review: All volume-constrained optimal sets and k>=3 are required, with continuity/Lipschitz alternatives. Regularity for the first eigenfunction does not handle higher multiplicity or the unknown optimal boundary.

statement: “Whatever aspect one takes into account, an open question is how to evaluate responses or reactions of teachers on given test items.”
technical_review: A question about evaluating teachers reactions supplies neither a formal mathematical proposition nor quantified success criterion. No full-scope theorem certificate can be inferred.

statement: Let $G$ be a finite group with a normal $p$-subgroup $N$, and let $u$ be a torsion unit in $\mathbb{Z}G$ which maps to the identity under the map $\mathbb{Z}G \to \mathbb{Z}(G/N)$. Is $u$ conjugate to an element of $N$ by a unit of $\mathbb{Z}_pG$, where $\mathbb{Z}_p$ denotes the ring of $p$-adic integers?
technical_review: Every finite group, normal p-subgroup and augmentation-kernel torsion unit is quantified with integral p-adic conjugacy. Modular eigenvalue tests do not construct the required unit conjugator; strong p-adic rigidity prior must be audited before any investment.

statement: For the problem $(P)$ described in the report, does the optimal control necessarily have the Lipschitz regularity known in the case where the optimal state is active at only finitely many points? The report answers negatively: it gives a counterexample with a linear elliptic equation in which the optimal control is not Lipschitz.
technical_review: The statement explicitly says the report provides a linear elliptic counterexample to Lipschitz control. Rebuilding a reported example would not earn novelty credit; actual body not audited.

statement: Let $G=\operatorname{Homeo}(D^2,\partial D^2,\mathrm{Area})$ be the group of area-preserving homeomorphisms of the $2$-disc that are the identity in some neighbourhood of the boundary. Is $G$ a simple group?
technical_review: This is the full simplicity question for compactly supported area-preserving disc homeomorphisms. Known nonsimplicity literature is a serious prior lead, not body-cleared evidence here; no new subgroup construction is proposed.

statement: Let $M^d$ be a triangulated $d$-manifold (simply connected, closed) with a discrete metric such that the discrete curvature (angle defect) along any $(d-2)$-simplex is positive. Give a discrete proof that $M^d$ is homeomorphic to $S^d$. (Or give a counterexample.)
technical_review: All dimensions with positive codimension-two angle defects and simply connected closed topology are quantified. A two-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet argument does not extend to a discrete sphere theorem in this scope.

statement:
For a bounded planar domain $\Omega$ with area $A$, let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be the first two positive Neumann eigenvalues, and let $D$ be the unit disk. Prove or disprove
\[
A\sqrt{\mu_1(\Omega)\mu_2(\Omega)}\le \pi\mu_1(D),
\]
with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a disk.
technical_review: Primary report p.405 explicitly asks this geometric-mean bound and separates it from the weaker harmonic-mean theorem and the triangle-only result. Those results do not subsume it. No arbitrary-domain Rayleigh test mechanism controlling the product with the sharp constant and equality case was found.

statement: Does derandomizing polynomial identity testing for depth-4 multilinear arithmetic circuits imply a derandomization of PIT for general multilinear arithmetic circuits?
technical_review: A derandomization transfer for all multilinear circuits is required. Existing generic depth reduction can destroy multilinearity or incur unsuitable size; no reduction with the necessary quantitative resource bound is supplied.

statement: Can a counterexample to Naimark’s problem be constructed using \[31mZFC+CH\[0m, or using \[31mZFC\[0m alone?
technical_review: Either ZFC+CH or ZFC construction of a Naimark counterexample requires exact operator-algebra and set-theoretic hypotheses. A construction under a different additional principle would not answer the stated alternatives.

statement: Give an explicit example of a billiard with a cusp on the boundary such that reflections accumulate at the tip in finite time.
technical_review: Primary report p.961 defines planar piecewise-smooth billiards and elastic reflections, then requests finite-time cusp accumulation. Prescribing a summable polygonal path alone does not give smooth finite boundary arcs with the correct normals and no intervening collisions. No verified example; no successor or full billiard-dependency audit.

statement:
Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be the elliptic curve defined by
\[
x-\frac1x+y-\frac1y=2.
\]
The report states the identity
\[
m\left(x+\frac1x+y+\frac1y-\sqrt{-4}\right)\doteq L'_{E/\mathbb Q}(0),
\]
where, for \(P\in\mathbb C[x,y]\) as written in the report,
\[
m(P)=(2\pi i)^{-2}\int_{|x|=|y|=1}\log|P(x,y)|\,\frac{dx}{x}\frac{dy}{y}.
\]
technical_review: The report states an identity with a dotted equality whose normalization is not defined in the record. Numerical Mahler-measure agreement cannot determine its exact rational factor or prove the L-value identity.

statement: If $M$ is a compact $3$-manifold and $\gamma \in \pi_1(M) \setminus \{1}$, there exists a finite commutative ring $R$ with identity and a homomorphism $\rho:\pi_1(M)\to \operatorname{PSL}(2,R)$ such that $\rho(\gamma)$ is a non-identity element.
technical_review: Every nonidentity element of every compact 3-manifold group needs a separating PSL(2,R) representation over a finite commutative ring. Residual finiteness into arbitrary finite groups does not give this restricted representation class; known residual-PSL2 objections need actual body audit.

statement:
Let $X$ be a complex projective K3 surface and let $f:X\to X$ be a symplectic automorphism of finite order, meaning that $f^*\sigma=\sigma$ for a nonzero regular two-form $\sigma$ on $X$. Then the induced action
\[
f^*:\operatorname{CH}^2(X)\to\operatorname{CH}^2(X)
\]
is the identity.
technical_review: All projective K3 surfaces and finite-order symplectic automorphisms are required. This is a strong known-theorem lead in the K3 Chow-action literature; no body or dependency replay here and no new claim.

statement: For one cap size in dimension $n=3$ (that is, $N=1$), the semidefinite-programming upper bound for spherical cap packing density and Florian’s geometric upper bound appear to meet for infinitely many cap angles as the angle decreases. Prove or disprove that these two bounds meet infinitely often.
technical_review: Infinitely many angles require an analytic characterization of the one-cap SDP bound and exact Florian contacts, not numerical near-coincidences or finitely many angles. Those formulas are not present in the record.

statement: Prove or disprove the existence of infinitely many knots \(\{K_n\}\) whose ropelength grows faster than \(O(\operatorname{Cr}(K_n))\).
technical_review: Needs an infinite knot family with unbounded ropelength/crossing ratio. A large single example or superlinear upper bound is irrelevant; no lower-bound mechanism beating linear crossing growth is identified.

statement: For a positive quaternionic Kähler manifold $M$ of quaternionic dimension $n\ge 2$ and positive scalar curvature $\kappa>0$, can one prove sufficiently many relations among the four characteristic numbers $\langle u^n,[M]\rangle$, $\langle u_1u^{n-1},[M]\rangle$, $\langle u_1^2u^{n-2},[M]\rangle$, and $\langle u_2u^{n-2},[M]\rangle$ to prove the Salamon conjecture by the displayed identity?
technical_review: All positive quaternionic Kahler manifolds and enough characteristic-number relations to force Salamon are required. Manipulating the displayed identity without geometric restrictions cannot supply those relations.

statement: Sarason conjectured that the full Poisson $A_2$ condition would be sufficient for the two-weight inequality for the Hilbert transform. The report states that F. Nazarov disproved this conjecture by a counterexample.
technical_review: The literal statement explicitly attributes a counterexample to Nazarov. Reconstructing a reported disproof is ineligible; no proof-body replay or chronology clearance claimed.

statement: The assertion that every increasing map $f:D\cap[0,1]\to D\cap[0,1]$, where $D$ is the set of finite decimal numbers, has a fixed point is false: the report states that a counterexample was found.
technical_review: The literal statement reports that the finite-decimal fixed-point assertion is false. An elementary jump across a nondecimal cut would be a classical order-incompleteness construction, not a new eligible outcome.

statement:
Bass conjectured that for a commutative noetherian ring $R$, without assuming that $R$ has many units, the relative homotopy groups satisfy
\[
\pi_i\bigl(BGL_n^+(R),BGL_{n-1}^+(R)\bigr)=0\qquad\text{for }i\le n-\operatorname{sr}(R).
\]
The report states that this general conjecture is false, with $R=\mathbb Z$ already providing a counterexample.
technical_review: The literal statement reports a Z counterexample to the general Bass stability assertion. Proving the same failure is not new; source counterexample body and relative-homotopy computations not replayed.

statement:
Let $m=(m_1,\dots,m_n)$ be a Hessenberg function, meaning $m_1\le \dots\le m_n$ and $i\le m_i\le n$, and let $y\in\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rs}}$ be regular semisimple. For the graph $G(m)$ and Hessenberg variety $H(m,y)$ defined in the report, the Shareshian–Wachs identity is
\[
\omega X_{G(m)}(t)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z} t^k\,\operatorname{ch} H^{2k}(H(m,y)).
\]
technical_review: All Hessenberg functions and regular semisimple y are quantified in the Shareshian-Wachs identity. Existing proof literature is an immediate prior lead; no fresh full cohomological construction or body audit here.

statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak n)$ be a local ring and $J$ a perfect ideal of $T$. Then $e(T) \le e(T/J)$.

Here the report further states that Conjecture 4 implies Lech’s conjecture, that no counterexample was known, and that the claim remains unresolved even when $J$ is $\mathfrak n$-primary.
technical_review: All local rings and perfect ideals are quantified; even the primary ideal case is included. Regular or complete-intersection special cases do not establish this multiplicity inequality at full scope.

statement: For the surface groups, namely the fundamental groups of orientable 2-manifolds, there is a finite algorithm that determines, for any finite product of generators and inverse generators (a word), whether that word represents the identity in the group.
technical_review: The literal target is the classical word-problem algorithm for orientable surface groups. A Dehn reduction or the abelian low-genus algorithms would be known proofs and receive no discovery credit; no new theorem proposed.

statement: Classify simple transitive 2-representations for fiat 2-categories with only one left and one right (non-identity) cell.
technical_review: A classification for all fiat 2-categories of the specified cell type requires a structural parametrization and completeness theorem. A single cell representation example is not a full answer.

statement: Assuming the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH), prove that for some constant $\varepsilon>0$, approximating the Bichromatic Closest Pair problem under the Euclidean metric within a factor of $3$ requires time $\Omega(N^{1+\varepsilon})$.
technical_review: Requires a quantitative SETH reduction for factor-3 Euclidean bichromatic approximation. Ambient dimension, randomized/deterministic model and approximation convention must be sourced; arbitrary metric gadgets do not automatically embed with this gap.

statement: **Problem 1.** Prove or disprove that Lipschitz minimizers are $C^1$ in dimension $n\ge 3$ when $D_F$ consists of finitely many points.
technical_review: All dimensions n>=3 and finite degeneracy sets are required. Uniform ellipticity estimates do not remain uniform at the degenerate gradient values; no counterexample satisfying the finite-set constraint supplied.

statement:
For the RT and dual BC discretizations described in the report, the proposed stabilization relies on the identity
$$P_{\Sigma}^{H}\left(\frac{G^{T}}{2}-K_{ik}\right)G^{-T}\left(\frac{G^{T}}{2}+K_{k}\right)P_{\Lambda}^{H}=0.$$
technical_review: Requires the precise RT/dual-BC discretizations and all indicated projections and matrices. Assigning arbitrary matrices to falsify the displayed product would not respect these constraints and is not a valid counterexample.

statement: Prove that the upper and lower bounds in (6), namely $\mu_h \le \|\nabla(u-u_h)\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le \eta_h$ (up to data oscillation terms), are equivalent, at least up to oscillation terms.
technical_review: An error sandwiched between two estimators does not by itself make the estimators comparable. Efficiency/reliability, oscillation terms and mesh-uniform constants need the full BEM construction; none proved here.

statement:
Consider the integration problem for the class $\bar C^2(D_d)=\{f\in C^2(D_d)\mid \|f\|_\infty\le 1,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\le d^{-1/2},\ \operatorname{Lip}(D_\Theta f)\le d^{-1}\}$. Prove or disprove the conjecture that there exists a constant $C>0$, independent of $d$ and $D_d$, such that

$$e_n(\bar C^2(D_d),\mathrm{INT})\ge C\,n^{-2/d}.$$
technical_review: Primary pp.386-387 impose bounded Lipschitz volume-one domains, define minimal error over n function values, and give cube/grid-only sharpness. A shrinking-domain counterexample is a scope error. No domain- and dimension-uniform fooling-function argument satisfying both Lipschitz derivative scales was established.

statement: For a fixed 4-manifold $M$, what are the homotopy types of $\mathrm{Homeo}_{\partial}(M)$ and $\mathrm{Diff}_{\partial}(M)$? Here $\mathrm{Homeo}_{\partial}(M)$ and $\mathrm{Diff}_{\partial}(M)$ are the topological groups of homeomorphisms and diffeomorphisms of $M$ that restrict to the identity on the boundary, equipped respectively with the compact-open and Whitney topologies.
technical_review: All fixed 4-manifolds are covered by a request for homotopy types of two infinite-dimensional groups. Ball or special simply connected cases cannot answer this general classification.

statement:
Let $V=\mathbb{C}^d$ with $d
greater than or equal to 5$, and let $G$ be one of $\mathrm{GL}(V)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(V)$, or $\mathrm{GO}(V)$. Let $X\leq G$ be a Zariski-closed subgroup whose identity component $X^{\circ}$ is reductive. If
$$M_8(X,V)=M_8(G,V),$$
then $X$ is big, i.e. $X\geq [G,G]$.
technical_review: Full eighth-moment equality rigidity for the three classical groups and reductive identity component is required. Larsen/Guralnick-Tiep moment literature is a strong known-result lead; no proof-body audit or new certificate supplied.

statement: Prove or refute the conjecture attributed to Kevin Costello that, for the noncommutative resolved-conifold case, the partially fermionized cohomological Hall algebra/Yangian obtained from the modified tripled-quiver potential is the Yangian associated to \(\mathfrak{gl}(1|1)\).
technical_review: The modified potential and fermionization conventions determine the algebra. Matching a few generators or low-degree dimensions would not prove the required full Yangian isomorphism.

statement: For which closed, spin, simply connected, smooth 4-manifolds $X$ is the Dehn twist $t_X$ smoothly isotopic to the identity?
technical_review: A classification of closed spin simply connected smooth four-manifolds by Dehn-twist triviality is required. A single family or obstruction does not settle all X; no short complete classification route.

statement:
Let $D$ be the unit square. Prove that for any convex subdomain $\a9 \\D$, one has
$$
\mu_2(\Omega)\ge \mu_2(D).
$$
technical_review: The convex-subdomain relation is corrupted in the record. Even interpreting it as inclusion in the square, standard diameter bounds lose a factor and do not yield the sharp square constant; no source or successor body read.

statement: What about the remaining families of finite groups of Lie type: how long is a shortest mixed identity in this case?
technical_review: Remaining families refers to source-dependent exclusions, and shortest mixed identity requires coefficient and length conventions. A fixed finite-group word search supplies only parameter cases and cannot determine family asymptotics.
